reason: The hidden truth marks TVs as outside the 9-family service, and Conversation 1 did exactly what was expected: a prompt, honest out-of-scope statement, referral to the manufacturer or a specialist electronics repairer, and a clear warning not to open the case because of stored charge. Conversation 2 treated the TV as an in-scope diagnosis, buried the homeowner in long checklists, quoted US dollar prices before switching to pounds, and offered DIY LED-strip replacement with instructions to remove the back cover, which the ground truth lists as unsupported and which conflicts with the 'do not open the TV' safety boundary. Conversation 2 did correctly identify backlight failure via the torch test and eventually steered to a home-visit repairer once the customer refused to open it, so it was not useless, but it overstepped scope and briefly encouraged the one thing the homeowner should not do.
